plan: Store the workspace as a deep-copied plain-dict tree (`copy.deepcopy` on construction and in `to_data()`) so callers can never alias internal state.
Centralize tree walking in a recursive generator (`_iter_items`) used by both `total_word_count` and `unresolved_markers`, with containment defined by a `_CONTAINER_KINDS` set ({'section', 'group'}).

Tokenize note text with two compiled regexes: a marker pattern `\[\[\?(\w+)\]\]` whose matches are captured for unresolved identifiers and replaced with a space before word counting, and `\b\w+\b` for maximal word runs; references contribute their declared `word_count` and `unresolved` list directly.
Render `outline()` by emitting the workspace title, then a depth-first walk appending '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' per item, with top-level items at depth 1.

Implement `move` as validate-then-mutate: resolve the moved item plus its parent list (`_find_with_parent`), resolve the destination list (`_container_items`, honoring the literal 'workspace'), reject non-string ids, missing ids, non-container destinations, out-of-range indices, and self/descendant containment (`_contains`) — all before any mutation, so any `ValueError` leaves `to_data()` byte-identical.
Remove the moved item from its parent list by object identity (`is`), then append or `insert` at the validated index, preserving the whole subtree.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at the construction and export boundaries
Recursive depth-first generator traversal over a kind-tagged dict tree
Compiled-regex marker extraction and marker-stripped word counting
Depth-indexed indentation rendering ('  ' * depth) for the outline
Identity-based parent-list lookup for structural edits
Full precondition validation before mutation (all-or-nothing move semantics)
Subtree containment check to forbid moving a container into itself or a descendant
